question: Should OpenClaw sponsor the RFC-backed experimental Claws lifecycle as a persistent core feature, including package-declared workspace-file writes and SQLite ownership provenance?
rationale: The patch is a coherent implementation slice, but accepting a new core mutation and recovery lifecycle is a product and ownership decision that code review cannot safely infer from the branch alone.

options.title: Sponsor the experimental core lifecycle
options.body: Accept the RFC direction and review this slice after its prerequisite stack, preserving the consent, fs-safe, and provenance boundaries.

options.title: Keep Claw packages external
options.body: Decline the core lifecycle direction and route any reusable package or workspace authoring capability through existing plugin or ClawHub seams.

options.title: Pause for a narrower charter
options.body: Request a maintainer-authored scope decision that defines which Claw resources, recovery guarantees, and long-term support commitments belong in core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the experimental core lifecycle
recommendation.body: Accept the RFC direction and review this slice after its prerequisite stack, preserving the consent, fs-safe, and provenance boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review feedback is the only concrete supplied maintainer-adjacent signal defining the required filesystem and identity invariants.
